one_liner: C/C++ compressor for arrays of fixed-size numeric elements that picks its own filter; claims better ratio and speed than Blosc2+Zstd.
what_it_does: Stenos compresses buffers of fixed-width records (integers, floats, structs of up to 65534 bytes per element) given the element size, much like Blosc, but without asking the caller to choose a shuffle filter. The C ABI has one-shot stenos_compress/stenos_decompress (level 0-9), a reusable context with thread count, level, superblock size and a time budget (stenos_set_max_nanoseconds), stenos_get_info for the stored decompressed size, random-access stenos_decompress_sub_part over a seekable stream, and stenos_guess_bytesoftype. It is not a drop-in for Blosc or zstd: the frame format is its own and the caller must pass the same element size to decompress.
how_it_is_fast: For each superblock it estimates compressibility (a write-free 'dry' LZ4 pass or a block size guess) and picks among four paths: a SIMD block codec, byte transposition (Blosc's shuffle code) plus Zstd, transposition plus byte delta plus Zstd, or raw Zstd. The SIMD block codec works on 256-element blocks, choosing per 16-element row between bit packing, delta coding and RLE with SSE4.1/AVX2 (BMI2 where available), and can hand residuals to Zstd at higher levels. Level 1 on multi-byte elements uses the block codec alone, which the README puts at about 2 GB/s compression and 3 GB/s decompression.
when_to_use: Compressing in-memory arrays of sensor samples, image or volume data, time series or float tables on x86-64 with SSE4.1/AVX2, where you would otherwise reach for Blosc + Zstd.
You do not know which filter (byte shuffle, bit shuffle, delta) suits the data and want the library to choose per superblock.
Hard latency budgets: the time-limited mode adjusts the level during compression and falls back to memcpy so a call finishes in roughly the requested time.
Large compressed arrays on slow storage where you need only some element ranges back (stenos_decompress_sub_part skips untouched superblocks).
Multi-threaded block compression of big buffers via stenos_set_threads.
when_not_to_use: General byte streams such as text or logs: it targets typed arrays, and plain zstd or LZ4 is the simpler choice there.

ARM or other non-x86 targets when speed matters: block compression is disabled under NEON ('Disable block compression on ARM for now' in stenos.cpp), leaving only the shuffle+Zstd paths, which is roughly what Blosc2 already offers.
Streaming compression: the README says it is not supported yet.

When you need interoperable or long-lived files read by other tools: the format is Stenos-only, the project has no tagged releases and 18 stars, and a container class (cvector) was pulled in September 2026 because it 'needs corrections first'.
When you need independent proof of the speed claims: the only benchmark is the author's own, timing compression only.

integration.dependencies: Zstd (fetched and built by default via FetchContent); OpenCL SDK fetched by default for the bundled video codec unless STENOS_WITH_OPENCL=OFF; bundles Blosc shuffle code, a simplified LZ4 and sse2neon
integration.min_toolchain: README says C++14, but CMakeLists.txt sets cxx_std_17; CMake 3.16+
integration.platforms: x86-64 with SSE4.1 for the SIMD block codec (AVX2 used when present); other Zstd-supported platforms, including ARM, run without the block codec; CI builds Windows/MSVC, Linux/GCC and macOS/Clang
integration.thread_safety: Documented: one context must not be used from several threads without external locking; different contexts may run in parallel. Internally a context can use multiple worker threads.
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial: same role and element-size parameter as Blosc's typesize, but a different API and an incompatible frame format

gotchas: The CMake option STENOS_NATIVE_ARCH defaults to ON and adds -march=native (and -mno-avx512f off macOS), so a default build may not run on older CPUs; turn it off for distributable binaries.

The README lists STENOS_BUILD_ZSTD as OFF by default, but CMakeLists.txt defaults it to ON, so a default build fetches and statically links its own Zstd instead of the system one; STENOS_WITH_OPENCL is also ON by default and pulls the Khronos OpenCL SDK.
bytesoftype is not stored in the frame: decompressing with a different element size than the compressor used is a caller error.
Compressed data from an x86 SIMD build decodes on non-SSE machines through a scalar block_decompress path, but compression there never uses the block codec, so ratio and speed differ by platform.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick Stenos over plain Zstandard or LZ4 when the input is an array of fixed-width numbers on x86-64 and you want transposition, delta and bit packing chosen automatically; for byte streams, on ARM, or when you need a stable widely supported format, Zstandard or LZ4 remain the safer choices.
verified_claims_summary: The author's own benchmark (benchs/bench_to_csv.cpp, single thread, Intel Core i7-10850H with AVX2, compiler and flags unstated) times compression only at levels 1-9 against Blosc2 byte shuffle + Zstd and Blosc2 bitshuffle + Zstd on 10 to 12 files from the stenos_dataset repo, and docs/benchmarks.svg plots ratio against compression speed with no numeric table. The README's '2GB/s compress, 3GB/s decompress' for the block codec and its 'or lz4' comparison are not backed by published numbers; the Blosc2+LZ4 variants in bench_all.cpp are commented out and decompression is not timed.
status_note: Actively developed (146 commits, last 2026-09-21) and MIT-licensed, but young, single-author, with no releases and few users; vendor it only with your own round-trip tests.
